title: Arbitrary-precision residual eigensolve on the fixed rounded graph
question: After the R-426 row is reconstructed from the declared double-precision graph snapshot, does an arbitrary-precision basis-invariant residual eigensolve remove the 5e-7 residual-reuse mismatch?

new_perspective.principle: Separate upstream source-rounding uncertainty from downstream eigensolver conditioning by converting the fixed graph and weights to Decimal arithmetic and solving every residual compression with a deterministic high-precision symmetric Jacobi routine.
route: Reconstruct the R-426 row and retain its float graph weights and conductances as exact decimal input strings; do not change beta, orientation, cutoff, row, tail rule or comparison tolerance.
Construct two independent Decimal orthonormal bases of the same blockwise weighted-zero-mean residual subspace: anchor-elimination Gram-Schmidt and projected-standard-vector Gram-Schmidt.
Diagonalize both Decimal residual compressions with 80-digit precision and a 1e-60 Jacobi stopping threshold, then compare the resulting invariant gaps with the R-422 and R-426 fixed values.
Classify only the rounded-input finite boundary. The upstream Gibbs/coordinate diagonalization and an interval enclosure for the original real inputs remain separate missing assumptions.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A precision uplift can distinguish a finite algebraic residual mismatch from downstream floating-point sensitivity; it cannot provide a common unbounded core, a regulator limit, a physical sector or a Yang-Mills statement.

precision_contract.input_mode: R-428 double-precision graph values converted from canonical decimal strings

assumptions: The R-428 reconstruction is the declared fixed finite source snapshot for this downstream precision audit.
Converting each finite float to its canonical decimal string and using Decimal arithmetic isolates downstream eigensolver error but does not recover uncomputed upstream digits.
The blockwise weighted-zero-mean constraints define one residual subspace for the fixed positive graph.
The 5e-7 R-426 comparison tolerance and fixed row are immutable.
The Decimal Jacobi residual is treated as numerically converged only at the rounded-input level; no interval enclosure is asserted.
missing_assumptions: Arbitrary-precision or interval-certified reconstruction of the Gibbs state, coordinate eigenbasis and graph weights from the original Hamiltonian.
A rigorous enclosure that propagates upstream input uncertainty through the conditional row and residual operator.
A basis-independent exact or rigorously bounded residual-reuse value for the original unrounded model.
A common unbounded Q3 Hamiltonian core, regulator/volume-uniform estimate and history/OS/KMS/GNS/physical-sector transfer.
stop_conditions: If the two Decimal bases disagree beyond 1e-50 after Jacobi convergence, classify the precision lane as a construction failure and retain R-428.
If the Decimal invariant gap agrees with R-422 within 5e-7, do not claim repair without an upstream source enclosure.
Never change the R-426 comparison tolerance, clip the residual, or promote a rounded-input finite result to a uniform or physical theorem.
evidence_level: T0 / EXECUTED 80-DIGIT DECIMAL DOWNSTREAM PRECISION UPLIFT ON THE FIXED R-428 GRAPH SNAPSHOT; upstream source uncertainty remains open
non_claims: No exact certification of the original Gibbs/coordinate inputs.
No repair or closure of the R-426 residual-reuse route for the original unrounded model.
No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform Schur/residual bound.
No common core, history transfer, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, sector gap or continuum limit.
No C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
boundary: R-429 can certify a basis-invariant residual value only for the decimalized R-428 finite graph snapshot. Any mismatch with R-422 therefore identifies a rounded-input algebraic boundary, while the original source-rounding enclosure remains missing.
next_unlock: Propagate arbitrary-precision or interval arithmetic through the original Hamiltonian Gibbs state, coordinate diagonalization and projected graph before deciding whether the R-426 mismatch survives the unrounded input uncertainty.

lean_crosscheck.role: R429 Lean checks only the scalar decimal-gap separation and finite-scope inequalities; Decimal matrix arithmetic remains executable Python.
